title: Map of Africa in 1914
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lesson 21 (Map of Africa in 1914 (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 21: A little history: Africa's past, colonialism and independence. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Use the atlas map on the slides: colour the colonies of Britain and France in 1914. By 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia were independent.

panels.title: Trade and the slave trade
points: The transatlantic slave trade took millions

bullets: By 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia were independent

model.title: How did colonial borders cause problems?

parts.text: Cause: borders drawn in Europe with straight lines
They split some peoples and joined rivals
Consequence: disputes and conflicts after independence
Link: some borders still argued over today

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A linked cause and consequence explanation

keywords.def: a land ruled by a king or queen
a land ruled by another country
one country taking control of another
European countries dividing Africa, about 1880 to 1914

questions.a: A meeting of European powers (1884 to 1885) that set rules for dividing Africa
Egypt, Aksum, Mali, Songhai, Great Zimbabwe

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box, explain two ways colonialism affected Africa (Point, Evidence, Explain).
questions.a: Two PEE points, e.g. borders and conflict; economies built for export of raw materials

questions.q: Extend: On the map, colour the colonies of Britain and France in 1914.
questions.a: Accurate colouring using the atlas map

questions.q: Stretch: Why might people in Africa today see colonial history differently from people in Britain?
questions.a: Different experiences: loss of land and freedom versus national pride

questions.q: By 1914, which African countries were still independent?
questions.a: B) Ethiopia and Liberia. Only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent of European rule.

questions.q: Big question: how did Europe come to rule Africa?
questions.a: Through trade, then conquest, agreed at the Berlin Conference, helped by weapons and divisions
